item.title: MiniMax publishes AI-discovered cryptographic attacks with papers and code
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: MiniMax has published research showing how an internal AI model helped discover attacks against experimental cryptographic schemes and solve previously unanswered public challenges. The company announced the work on Sunday, following the release of technical papers and supporting code on November 20. The results span encryption, digital signatures and hash functions. In the TII McEliece […]
item.content:encoded:
MiniMax has published research showing how an internal AI model helped discover attacks against experimental cryptographic schemes and solve previously unanswered public challenges. The company announced the work on Sunday, following the release of technical papers and supporting code on November 20.

The results span encryption, digital signatures and hash functions. In the TII McEliece challenge, MiniMax reports recovering 94 private keys, including 55 instances without previously published solutions, with speedups of up to 43,400 times over existing implementations. Other findings include practical attacks on selected signature schemes and reduced-round versions of the ARADI block cipher.

MiniMax says the findings primarily originated from its internal model and were organized and verified by its research team. The published work concerns specific research designs, historical competition candidates and challenge parameters; it does not establish attacks on mainstream standards such as AES, RSA or SHA-256. The repository includes papers and code for examining the individual results. [MiniMax]

item.title: Huawei’s OSTA brand reportedly plans tablets, laptops and wearables
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Huawei’s new OSTA consumer brand is preparing to expand beyond smartphones into tablets, laptops and wearable devices, according to Chinese technology tipster Digital Chat Station. A compact tablet is already planned, the tipster said on Monday, following the launch of OSTA’s first handset, the O1 Pro, last week. The tipster described OSTA as a brand […]
item.content:encoded:
Huawei’s new OSTA consumer brand is preparing to expand beyond smartphones into tablets, laptops and wearable devices, according to Chinese technology tipster Digital Chat Station. A compact tablet is already planned, the tipster said on Monday, following the launch of OSTA’s first handset, the O1 Pro, last week.

The tipster described OSTA as a brand focused on experimental technology, with initial products expected to draw heavily on existing Huawei designs before moving toward independently developed devices. Its planned lineup is reportedly positioned in the midrange and premium segments. Huawei has not announced the additional products or their release schedules.

OSTA debuted with the O1 Pro, a wide-screen phone featuring the Kirin 9030S processor and an AI-focused edition of HarmonyOS 7. Expanding into other device categories would give Huawei’s new brand a broader role across its consumer hardware ecosystem. [IT Home, in Chinese]

The enclosed machine, labeled S01, uses six print heads. Booth staff confirmed to specialist outlet Nanjixiong that it was a product from the smartphone maker, although a formal announcement was still […]
item.content:encoded:
Honor has displayed a consumer 3D printer prototype at the Formnext exhibition in Frankfurt, giving an early look at its expansion into desktop manufacturing. The enclosed machine, labeled S01, uses six print heads. Booth staff confirmed to specialist outlet Nanjixiong that it was a product from the smartphone maker, although a formal announcement was still pending.

According to specifications displayed beside the machine, the S01 has a build volume of 270 × 270 × 270 millimeters and a maximum printing speed of 1,000 millimeters per second. Its multiple print heads support printing with different materials or colors without relying on a single nozzle to handle every change.

Honor has not announced a retail price or release date. The prototype brings the company into a consumer hardware category already contested by Chinese manufacturers including Bambu Lab and Creality, where printing reliability, software and material handling are central parts of the product experience. [Nanjixiong, in Chinese]

item.title: Ant Group leads $100 million round in humanoid startup Simplexity Robotics
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics has raised $100 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group, valuing the company at $1.6 billion, chairman and co-founder Wang Kai told Bloomberg. Existing investors including Tencent, HSG and Lanchi Ventures also participated. Founded by former Li Auto executives, Simplexity is developing embodied AI and robots that […]
item.content:encoded:
Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics has raised $100 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group, valuing the company at $1.6 billion, chairman and co-founder Wang Kai told Bloomberg. Existing investors including Tencent, HSG and Lanchi Ventures also participated.

Founded by former Li Auto executives, Simplexity is developing embodied AI and robots that can perform tasks in physical environments. Its latest product, a wheeled humanoid called iX, was unveiled on Monday with demonstrations including preparing and delivering drinks, fetching objects and guiding visitors.

The financing adds Ant to the company’s investor base as Chinese technology groups expand their involvement in robotics. Simplexity is pursuing service tasks that require a combination of perception, navigation and manipulation, bringing its automotive engineering background into competition with established humanoid developers. [Bloomberg]

item.title: Xiaomi reportedly hires former Xpeng Europe executive ahead of 2027 car launch
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Xiaomi has hired former Xpeng Western and Southern Europe managing director Qiang Shunqiang to lead its European car business, Jiemian reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Qiang joined in September as managing director of Europe within Xiaomi’s international automotive business and is based in Germany. Xiaomi did not respond to the outlet’s request for […]
item.content:encoded:
Xiaomi has hired former Xpeng Western and Southern Europe managing director Qiang Shunqiang to lead its European car business, Jiemian reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Qiang joined in September as managing director of Europe within Xiaomi’s international automotive business and is based in Germany. Xiaomi did not respond to the outlet’s request for comment.

Qiang helped build Xpeng’s overseas sales and service network after joining the company in 2019. His arrival follows that of former Xpeng Northern Europe executive Jens Olsen, who joined Xiaomi in September to oversee Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.

The appointments add regional operating experience as Xiaomi prepares to begin overseas car sales in the third or fourth quarter of 2027, starting with Germany. Its European preparations also include a Munich research and design center led by former BMW M executive Rudolf Dittrich, alongside work on local distribution, delivery and after-sales services. Right-hand-drive markets are scheduled to follow in the first half of 2028. [Jiemian, in Chinese]

Announced at the Afu healthcare ecosystem conference, the devices are designed to track sleep, heart rate, breathing and blood oxygen levels, with AI-generated health reports and suggestions based on the readings. The wristband, called […]
item.content:encoded:
Ant Group’s AI health service Afu unveiled a smart ring and wristband on Monday, extending its health-management offering into wearable hardware. Announced at the Afu healthcare ecosystem conference, the devices are designed to track sleep, heart rate, breathing and blood oxygen levels, with AI-generated health reports and suggestions based on the readings.

The wristband, called Fuhuan in Chinese, comes in versions with and without a screen. The Fujie ring has a simple silver-white design. Ant highlighted long battery life for both products but did not disclose detailed battery specifications, retail prices or launch dates in the announcement.

Afu said the products would be open to cooperation with partners. The devices give the service a way to collect ongoing health measurements alongside information users provide in conversations, extending its role from answering individual questions to monitoring changes over time. [Jiemian, in Chinese]

The model appeared in the service’s selection menu on Monday, where it is listed with vision support and a one-million-token context window. A member of Zhipu’s operations team said the company had been scaling both […]
item.content:encoded:
Zhipu has made GLM-5.4 available through its Coding Plan subscription service, adding visual understanding and stronger capabilities across coding-related tasks. The model appeared in the service’s selection menu on Monday, where it is listed with vision support and a one-million-token context window.

A member of Zhipu’s operations team said the company had been scaling both its model size and its Loop Transformer approach over the past three months. Subscribers on V2, V3 and team plans have received a 50% increase in their GLM-5.4 usage allowance and can access it by setting the model name to “glm-5.4.”

The rollout puts the new model directly into Zhipu’s developer subscription product. The company had not yet published a full technical introduction detailing its architecture, parameter count or benchmark results at the time of the report. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Do you really need an AI wearable to remember every moment?
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: Editor’s Note: Human memory is selective, while digital devices can capture far more than we can remember. Wearable AI cameras take this a step further, recording everyday moments and using AI to organize them into personal recaps and insights. Looki is among the startups exploring this idea with its wearable camera, the L1. Early reviews […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s Note: Human memory is selective, while digital devices can capture far more than we can remember. Wearable AI cameras take this a step further, recording everyday moments and using AI to organize them into personal recaps and insights. Looki is among the startups exploring this idea with its wearable camera, the L1. Early reviews point to both the appeal of revisiting forgotten moments and the challenges of making sense of them, from missed context to privacy concerns. Can AI make our memories more useful, and what trade-offs come with letting it document our lives?

Human memory is sometimes a poor recording device. A commute blurs, a conversation loses its edges, and small moments vanish before we know they mattered. What remains is selective, shaped by emotion as much as fact. The latest attempt to capture these fleeting moments comes in the form of wearable AI cameras. Looki’s L1 is one of a growing number of devices in this emerging category. It records snippets of daily life, which its app can later assemble into summaries, visual stories, and daily recaps.

A Day Recut—and Reassessed

In a review for GameRevolution, Mack Ashworth found that the L1 could turn daily footage into recap videos, though the results were not always consistent. Some compilations offered a good overview of his day, while others were so short that they contained little to revisit.

Tom’s Guide’s Elton Jones had a more entertaining experience during his two-week trial. The device captured scenes from his commute, workday and journey home, which the app turned into a daily vlog and a comic strip. Jones particularly enjoyed seeing ordinary moments, such as grabbing lunch, reimagined as comic-book panels.

Jones also tested the L1’s food-tracking feature. After observing his lunch habits, the device generated nutritional breakdowns, compared meals across several days and suggested dietary adjustments.

While Jones found the feedback useful, his experience also raises questions about how accurately a wearable camera can assess someone’s eating habits from visual information alone.

The Cost of Being Remembered

Automatic capture also creates social friction. Stein described feeling awkward in public and worrying that people nearby did not know they might be recorded. Bystanders have little control over whether their image or conversations enter someone else’s private archive.

Looki says the L1 is not continuous by default and that its Trust Light blinks while recording. Its support FAQ says footage stays on the device until users choose to sync. The company’s privacy policy says personal content is not used to train general AI models and can be deleted on request. Looki also says it completed a SOC 2 Type I audit in 2026 and is working toward Type II.

But these measures do not settle consent in shared spaces. Looki’s policy puts responsibility for obtaining permissions on users.

Different Ways to Remember

Looki is exploring one way to build a personal AI memory, using visual recordings to capture everyday scenes, from places and activities to objects and interactions. Its L1 turns these clips into searchable records, daily vlogs and comic-style recaps.

Other companies are approaching the idea through sound. Amazon’s Bee Frontier uses recorded conversations to generate summaries and reminders. Plaud’s NotePin S organizes meetings and conversations into transcripts and notes, while Omi makes recorded conversations searchable through an AI pendant.

The approaches reflect different ideas about personal AI: visual devices capture the places and activities that shape a day, while audio-based ones preserve its conversations.

But a fuller record doesn’t necessarily make for a fuller life. As AI moves deeper into our daily lives, do we really need it to remember everything—or is forgetting part of being human?

item.title: Tencent releases Hy4 model weights with million-token context
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Tencent released the weights of its flagship Hy4 AI model on Friday, allowing developers to download and deploy the model themselves. The release follows Hy4’s initial launch on November 4 and makes the flagship available under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use and modification. Hy4 supports text, image and video understanding, with a […]
item.content:encoded:
Tencent released the weights of its flagship Hy4 AI model on Friday, allowing developers to download and deploy the model themselves. The release follows Hy4’s initial launch on November 4 and makes the flagship available under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use and modification.

Hy4 supports text, image and video understanding, with a context window of about one million tokens. Its mixture-of-experts language backbone contains 770 billion parameters, with 49 billion activated for each token. Tencent says the model improves on Hy4 preview in instruction following, long-context understanding, extended tasks and research.

The model supports workflows spanning graphical interfaces and command-line tools, alongside frontend development, game development and office tasks. Tencent provides deployment instructions for vLLM and SGLang, as well as fine-tuning resources and a safety evaluation card. The flagship’s release follows the separate opening of the smaller Hy4 flash model. [Tencent]

item.title: Ex-Qwen chief’s Pragmatik Labs raises funding at $5 billion valuation
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Pragmatik Labs, the AI startup founded by former Alibaba Qwen leader Lin Junyang, has raised new funding at a $5 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The round raised tens of millions of dollars, with new investors including HyT Capital, CDH Investments and automaker Geely. The valuation is 2.5 […]
item.content:encoded:
Pragmatik Labs, the AI startup founded by former Alibaba Qwen leader Lin Junyang, has raised new funding at a $5 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The round raised tens of millions of dollars, with new investors including HyT Capital, CDH Investments and automaker Geely.

The valuation is 2.5 times the $2 billion assigned to the company during its first financing in August, when it raised several hundred million dollars. That round was co-led by Gaorong Ventures and HSG, with participation from Tencent and a Shanghai government-backed investment fund.

Lin left Alibaba in March and established the Shanghai-based company over the summer. Pragmatik is developing next-generation AI agents for digital and physical environments. Its founder previously helped lead development of Alibaba’s Qwen model family, giving the young research company a prominent technical pedigree as it competes for funding and talent in China’s AI market. [Bloomberg]
